shared_elements: upright rectangular carved stone slab/monolith standing in situ
carving in relief on a flat vertical face
animal or creature head in profile
horizontal band(s) of repeated motifs dividing the surface
loose stone rubble/blocks at the base
justification: Both are tall upright relief-carved stone slabs set among rubble, each organised into stacked horizontal bands with profile creature heads and a small anthropomorphic figure among them, which gives a comparable overall silhouette and vertical register logic. The decisive difference is density and manner: A is a sparse, shallow, rounded low relief with isolated motifs floating on a blank ground, while B is a densely packed, deeply modelled surface of tightly ordered rectangular glyph-like blocks framing a prominent frontal figure, and it is a line engraving rather than a photograph.
